title: Fear vs Greed: The Two Forces Behind Every Presale Purchase
seoTitle: Fear vs Greed: The 2 Forces Behind Every Presale Purchase
description: Every new construction purchase is a balance between fear of buying a vision and the greed of a good deal. Learn why certainty is what tips buyers to sign.
answer: Two forces drive every presale purchase: fear and greed. Fear, because the buyer is signing for a vision, not a finished building. Greed, because presale prices are usually lower than similar properties on the market, and the home is brand new. The balance between them decides how fast people sign, and certainty is what tips it toward a sale.
keywords: how to sell presale units faster
body:
Anyone who has bought, or tried to sell, a home that does not exist yet knows the feeling. The buyer wants it, and the buyer is afraid of it, at the same time. In my experience, those two feelings explain almost everything about how fast a presale moves.

## The first force: fear

When you sign for new construction, you are not buying a building. You are buying a vision. There is nothing to walk through, nothing to touch, and a lot of time between the signature and the keys. Fear is the natural reaction to that gap. It is not a sign that the buyer is not interested. It is a sign that the buyer is being asked to trust something they cannot see.

## The second force: greed

At the same moment, the buyer is thinking that this could be one of the best deals of their life. And there is a reason for that feeling. When you buy pre-construction, you usually get access to a lower price than similar properties already on the market. On top of that, the home is brand new. A better price on a newer product is a strong pull.

## Why the balance decides the speed of the sale

Every presale buyer sits somewhere between these two forces. When greed is stronger, people sign quickly. When fear is stronger, they wait, ask for more time, or walk away. Seen from the buyer side, this balance decides how fast the contract gets signed. Seen from the developer side, it decides how fast the units sell.

This is why two projects with similar prices can sell at very different speeds. The price is only one side of the scale.

## Certainty is what tips the scale

A developer cannot do much to make a good price feel better than it already is. What a developer can do is reduce fear. The way to reduce fear is to deliver certainty: show the buyer as clearly as possible what they are actually getting, so the vision feels less like a promise and more like a known product.

In my view, delivering certainty is one of the most important things a developer can do to turn interest into sales. Interest is already there when someone asks about a presale. Certainty is what converts it.

## What this means if you are buying

If you are the buyer, it helps to name the two forces in yourself. Ask what is making you excited, and ask what is making you nervous. Then look for clear answers to the things that make you nervous before you sign. A good deal is only a good deal when you understand what you are buying.
takeaways: Every presale purchase is a balance between fear and greed.
Fear comes from buying a vision instead of a finished building.
Greed comes from a price that is usually lower than similar properties, on a brand new home.
The balance between the two decides how fast buyers sign and how fast units sell.
Delivering certainty reduces fear and is one of the strongest ways to turn interest into sales.
faq: Why are people afraid to buy pre-construction?
Because they are buying a vision rather than a finished building. There is nothing to walk through yet, so the buyer has to trust what they cannot see.
Buying before the building is finished usually gives access to a lower price than similar properties already on the market, and the buyer gets a brand new home.
How can a developer sell presale units faster?
By reducing fear rather than only cutting price. Delivering certainty, so buyers clearly understand what they are getting, helps convert interest into signed contracts.
What do fear and greed mean in real estate?
Fear is the worry about risk and the unknown. Greed is the pull of a good deal. In presales, the balance between them decides how quickly a buyer commits.
